hints: There are two different commits in this system. Name both.
This is a partitioned, replicated append-only log with consumer-group offsets and at-least-once delivery.
Key by order ID, ack after the in-sync replicas have the batch, commit offsets after processing, and route poison events to retry and dead-letter topics.

signals: Chooses the partition key for per-order ordering and sizes partitions from the slowest consumer group
Defines message commit as replicated to in-sync replicas and rejects unclean leader election for orders
Commits offsets after side effects and makes handlers idempotent
Isolates poison messages without stalling the partition and states the ordering cost
Distinguishes time-based retention from consumption and alerts on lag versus retention
followups: Finance needs each order counted exactly once in an external table. What can the log guarantee?
One merchant produces 30% of events. What happens to its partition?
Compare this to a per-message ack queue with visibility timeouts. When would you pick that?
